building.name: Transbay Terminal
building.architect: Timothy Pflueger and Arthur Brown, Jr.

historical_record.description: Turned into a regional bus depot, after the lower deck of the Bay Bridge was given over to cars in 1958 and the Key System dismantled.

Built as the Transbay Terminal to designs by Timothy Pflueger and Arthur Brown Jr., linked to the new Bay Bridge by a looping concrete viaduct that carried Key System trains into downtown. It was planned for 35 million passengers a year and handled 26 million at its wartime peak.

historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 4 that it may become eligible, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
historic_survey.note: Recorded as an individually significant building. The survey prints this building's address two ways: 425 Mission Street in one table and 401-25 Mission Street in another.
